subject: Sprint bridge: capacity reservation scenarios & close timeline
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Huang <linda@helixai.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sprint bridge: capacity reservation scenarios & close timeline

Linda —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We sketched a few runway options that line up with HelixAI's Q1 production ramp and your internal procurement windows. Sharing two capacity scenarios so we can converge on the MAP and an actionable close timeline:

Attachments: HelixAI_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (MAP draft), GPU_Tranche_Scenarios.pdf (sizing + lead times)

Quick summary:
- Scenario A (Conservative): 8x A100-equivalent slots initially, staggered tranches (50% canary -> 100% by week 6). Lower initial commit, shorter Dedicated lead time required.
- Scenario B (Aggressive): 16x slots up front (mix Dedicated + Private racks), 30% canary -> 100% by week 4. Requires earlier procurement kickoff and 8–10 week private lead time.

Key asks:
1) Which scenario aligns to your procurement cadence?
2) Any hard blackout dates for air-gapped/on-prem installs?
3) Can procurement confirm preferred payment/commit cadence (monthly vs quarterly)?

If you prefer, we can convert Scenario A into a 3-tranche financing approach to reduce upfront commitment. I’d like to get a MAP signed by end of November to hit a Jan production window.

Best —
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: HelixAI_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Linda Huang <linda@helixai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@helixai.com
Date: 2026-10-16T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sprint bridge: capacity reservation scenarios & close timeline

Diego —

Thanks for the crisp summary and the two scenarios. A few clarifying points from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement: our target is to finalize vendor selection by 2026-11-30; we prefer a staged commitment to match our budget cycle.
- Engineering: prefer Private racks for low-latency internal inference, but we need an initial Dedicated buffer while racks are installed.
- Can you confirm the real expected lead time for Private on-site racks (including network validation)? Earlier conversations mentioned 8–12 weeks.

Cc'ing procurement so they can confirm contract/PO timelines. We'll review the attached MAP and return redlines next week.

Thanks,
Linda Huang
Head of Platform
HelixAI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sprint bridge: capacity reservation scenarios & close timeline

Team —

Forwarding Linda's reply. Procurement asks and engineering preference point us to a hybrid plan: Dedicated buffer for Jan go-live, Private racks to follow. Can you review and propose:

- A tranche schedule that fits HelixAI's 11/30 vendor selection and our internal capacity build timelines.
- Concrete acceptance test windows (what do we need to sign off on during canary).
- A fallback model strategy in case initial quantized variants degrade across Helix's user mix.

Please annotate the MAP (HelixAI_MAP_v1.2.xlsx) with numbers and lead-time assumptions. Quick turnaround appreciated — Linda indicated redlines next week.

Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sprint bridge: capacity reservation scenarios & close timeline

Diego / team —

I've sketched a tranche schedule inside GPU_Tranche_Scenarios.pdf and summarized below (numbers are A100-equivalent slots):

Scenario H1 (staged hybrid):
- Tranche 1 (Canary): 6 slots on Dedicated (weeks 0–4) — objective: smoke + SLA validation (latency P95 target, KV cache hit rate)
- Tranche 2 (Partial private install): +8 slots private racks (weeks 6–10) — allow network validation and SOC2-specific audit checkpoints
- Tranche 3 (Scale to prod): +12 slots private (weeks 12–18) — full capacity for model M1 and M1-quant variants

Lead time notes:
- Dedicated buffer: 1–2 weeks to allocate (we can reserve immediately once MAP signed).
- Private rack procurement/ship + on-site plug: estimate 8–10 weeks given current vendor queues; network validation add 1 week.

Acceptance criteria (canary):
- 99% of requests return within agreed P95 latency ceiling across 95% of test prompts.
- Model quality regression < 2% measured on a supplied 2k prompt eval set (we’ll run evals nightly during canary).
- KV cache sustained hit rate > 65% for burst workloads.

Fallback plan: deploy a quantized-compatible variant for low-cost pathways but keep the full-precision model on Dedicated until regression testing clears.

I'll attach an annotated XLSX with exact dates tied to Helix's vendor selection timeline. I recommend we lock the MAP by 2026-11-24 to meet your 11/30 procurement checkpoint and give us runway for the private rack lead time to begin in early Dec if they award us the work.

- Marissa

[Attachment: GPU_Tranche_Scenarios.pdf (PDF)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sprint bridge: capacity reservation scenarios & close timeline

Quick technical notes from infra side:

- Quantization/variant impact: our tests show M1-8bit gives ~1.8x throughput improvement and ~5–7% quality delta on average prompts. For Helix's low-latency use case, recommend keeping 2–3 Dedicated full-precision nodes during initial canary to compare signals.
- KV cache warming: to meet the 65% hit rate we should pre-warm with the customer's top-10k prefix set; ask engineering to share query patterns by 11/10.
- Network validation checklist: need VLAN mapping, on-prem firewall rules, and a staging BGP session for private racks. Allocate one week in the MAP for this.

I'll add these specifics into the Acceptance-Test-Checklist.docx and flag any known blockers. Also recommend a 20% canary -> 60% -> 100% ramp (finer-grained than Marissa's 50/100) to reduce rollback blast radius.

—Karthik
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: procurement@helixai.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Sprint bridge: capacity reservation scenarios & close timeline — agreed milestones and next steps

Linda / Procurement —

Appreciate the review cycle. Based on your procurement window and our infra constraints, here's the consolidated ask and MAP milestones we propose (please confirm or mark redlines):

Milestone summary:
- 2026-11-24: Redwood MAP signature target (Helix preferred 11/30; we need 11/24 to lock Dedicated allocations)
- 2026-12-01: Begin Dedicated buffer allocation (6 slots) + kick-off private rack procurement
- 2027-01-10: Canary start (20% traffic to Dedicated buffer) — acceptance run 14 days
- 2027-02-15: Private racks on-site + network validation complete
- 2027-02-22: Gradual ramp (60% -> 100%) and final handover to Helix ops

Artifacts attached: HelixAI_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (annotated with dates), GPU_Tranche_Scenarios.pdf, Acceptance-Test-Checklist.docx

Immediate asks for procurement:
1) Can Helix confirm whether PO issuance will follow signature or require a separate master services agreement?
2) Please confirm any payment timing constraints that would affect the tranche schedule.

If those two items are green, we can finalize the MAP and I’ll drop a DocuSign link. Proposed slot reservation will be held for 72 hours after MAP signature to secure the Dedicated buffer.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-helixai-map

Shall we lock a 30-minute alignment call Wed 11/29 to walk the MAP and the acceptance checklist?

Best —
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
